content:
sam.chen: Heads up — seeing intermittent 502/503s from edge-ingress to inference-svc in us-west. Debug shows the service VIP resolving to different pod IPs on different edge nodes, and some nodes still hitting old pod IPs for headless endpoints. Anyone else seeing svc discovery weirdness?

maria.lewis: On it. Which cluster/pool is this happening in? dedicated or edge?

sam.chen: edge-pool-3 (gpu-edge-usw). A subset of nodes report stale endpoints.

derek.k: Could be EndpointSlice controller not syncing or kube-proxy not applying changes. Try: `kubectl get endpointslices -n inference -o wide` and `kubectl get pods -o wide -l app=inference` on one of the affected nodes.

sam.chen: Pasting a tiny snippet from an affected node's endpointslice output — notice missing endpoint for pod-7 on node-17:
```
NAME                        ADDRESSTYPE   ENDPOINTS
inference-abc-1234-xyz      IPv4          10.4.2.12,10.4.2.13
inference-abc-1234-node17   IPv4          10.4.2.12
```
We expected pod-7 (10.4.2.14) to be present on node-17 but it's not listed.

nora_p: We had a similar symptom when kube-proxy fell back from ipvs to iptables during a kernel upgrade and left stale conntrack state. This is TCP LB though — still possible. Any recent Calico/flannel changes?

sam.chen: We rolled Calico 3 days ago in that pool. Also noticed CoreDNS responses differ when queried from node vs from a pod — node DNS cache returned old cluster IP for the headless name. /etc/resolv.conf search order is slightly different on those nodes.

maria.lewis: Check kube-proxy logs for endpoint sync errors: `kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-proxy-<pod> | grep endpoint` — look for `Failed to sync endpointslice` or similar. Also check the endpoint controller logs.

sam.chen: kube-proxy log excerpt: `E1107 09:12:38.123456    1 endpoints.go:270] Failed to sync endpointslice inference/inference-abc-1234: timed out waiting for the condition`

infra-bot: Alert: endpoint_sync_errors detected on gpu-edge-usw node-17 (severity: warning) at 2024-11-07T09:12:40Z

derek.k: Short-term workaround: delete the affected EndpointSlice object(s) and let controller recreate them: `kubectl delete endpointslices <name> -n inference`. If it's kube-proxy specific, restarting the kube-proxy daemonset on the affected nodes helps. Also inspect conntrack for stale entries: `conntrack -L | grep 10.4.2.14`.

sam.chen: Deleting the endpointslice now and restarting kube-proxy on node-17. Will monitor metrics (5xx rate, latency). If it keeps flapping we'll roll back the calico upgrade on that pool.

maria.lewis: If this persists beyond ~30m and >5% error rate, create an incident and tag @oncall and networking. Add the outputs you just posted to the incident board.

sam.chen: Got it. Will update here with results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
